title: Build a startup in 24 hours: the Minimum MVP (headline, buy button, 1 feature)
summary: Marc argues founders overthink startups and burn months on features that earn nothing. Every startup has a 24-hour version: a headline, a buy button and one feature that solves the most painful problem. Everything invisible to the customer gets cut.

principles.text: We overthink startups: ship a minimal version in weeks, not months.
principles.quote: 20+ startups later and countless months spent on useless features, I can confidently say this: We overthink startups.

principles.text: Most effort has zero financial outcome, so months on one startup risks burnout; ship minimal instead.
principles.quote: Most of your efforts have 0 financial outcome—that’s entrepreneurship.

principles.text: Every startup has a 24-hour version; start from that baseline and add only the bare minimum.
principles.quote: there’s a version of your startup that can be published within 24 hours.

principles.text: A minimal MVP is a headline, a buy button, and one feature.
principles.quote: A headline, a buy button, and 1 feature.

principles.text: The headline matters most, like a YouTube thumbnail: people decide to invest time based on it.
principles.quote: Your headline is the most important. It’s like the thumbnail of a YouTube video

principles.text: Validate by getting paid; a waitlist is not enough, so include a buy button.
principles.quote: You can only validate an idea if people pay for it. A waitlist isn’t enough.
